title: test_nbr_health/test_neighbors_health: cSONiC neighbors classified as unknown (CsonicHost not recognized)
author: securely1g
body:
## Summary

The neighbor-health check in `tests/test_nbr_health.py` / `test_neighbors_health` dispatches only on `EosHost`/`SonicHost`. A `CsonicHost` is neither, so it falls through and the cSONiC neighbors are reported as unknown/unhealthy.

## Topology/Testbed

- **Topology:** t0
- **Testbed:** vms-kvm-t0-csonic
- **Neighbors:** cSONiC (docker-sonic-vs) neighbors

## Symptom/Error

Neighbor health dispatch only handles `EosHost`/`SonicHost`; `CsonicHost` falls through → neighbors reported unknown/unhealthy.

## Root cause

The neighbor-health check dispatches on `EosHost`/`SonicHost` only; `CsonicHost` is neither, so it is not recognized.

## Proposed fix

Add `CsonicHost` handling to the neighbor health check (treat like SONiC: check bgp/teamd/container health via the `CsonicHost` shell interface).

Found via cSONiC PR-CI parity validation (full t0 run 2026-06-18).

comments.author: securely1g
comments.body:
### Identified — draft fix (not yet verified)

**Root cause:** the neighbor health-check dispatch does not recognize `CsonicHost`, so cSONiC neighbors are classified as `unknown` and their BGP facts are never gathered.

**Draft fix:** add a `CsonicHost` branch (a `check_csonic_bgp_facts` helper) so neighbor BGP facts are collected through the cSONiC path.

**Status:** drafted and compiles, but **not yet run** on the testbed. Will update once verified on the live cSONiC testbed.

comments.author: yyynini
comments.body:
### Closure recommendation and implementation evidence

**Recommendation: close this test gap as implemented.** The original failure was that `CsonicHost` was not recognized by the neighbor-health dispatch, so cSONiC neighbors were reported as unknown/unhealthy.

**Implementation evidence**
- [PR #26144](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/26144), merged **2026-08-28**, adds the explicit `CsonicHost` branch and routes it through the existing `check_sonic_bgp_facts` helper.
- [Reviewed source: cSONiC dispatch and final failure assertion](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/21ee7658f262f94760ec3a5a14b90a380ccb85e5/tests/test_nbr_health.py#L149-L166).
- [Reviewed source: BGP-summary health check](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/21ee7658f262f94760ec3a5a14b90a380ccb85e5/tests/test_nbr_health.py#L90-L98).
- The PR reports a live docker-sonic-vs run in which the new branch passed for the cSONiC neighbors that previously failed as unknown. The reviewer concern about the guarded import was resolved with a plain import before approval.

This addresses the core recognition/health-check integration requested here. The existing EOS and SonicHost branches remain unchanged. Management-IP/SNMP checks are intentionally not applied to docker-exec cSONiC neighbors; this does not claim new exhaustive teamd/container-health coverage.

This review checked the merged implementation and current source; it did not perform a new physical-testbed run. **This comment records the closure rationale only; the issue is being left open at this step.**

linkedPullRequests.title: [test_nbr_health] Recognize CsonicHost neighbors in health check
linkedPullRequests.author: securely1g
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

`tests/test_nbr_health.py::test_neighbors_health` dispatches neighbor health checks only on `EosHost` and `SonicHost`:

```python
if isinstance(nbrhost, EosHost):
    ...
elif isinstance(nbrhost, SonicHost):
    ...
else:
    failmsg = "neighbor type {} is unknown".format(k)
    fails.append(failmsg)
```

A cSONiC (`docker-sonic-vs`) neighbor is a `CsonicHost`, which extends `NeighborDevice` and is **not** a `SonicHost` subclass. So on a `vms-kvm-t0-csonic` testbed every cSONiC neighbor falls through to the `else` branch and the test fails with "neighbor type ... is unknown", even when the neighbor is perfectly healthy.

Fixes #25523.

#### How I did it

Added a `CsonicHost` branch before the `SonicHost` branch. cSONiC neighbors are reached via `docker exec` (no SSH/SNMP mgmt path), so the new `check_csonic_health()`:
- verifies the container is reachable through the `CsonicHost` shell interface, and
- reuses `check_sonic_bgp_facts()` to confirm BGP is up via `vtysh -c "show ip bgp sum"`.

The SNMP and mgmt-facts checks used for EOS/SONiC are intentionally not run for cSONiC, because those neighbors have no SNMP/mgmt-IP surface.

#### How to verify it

Run on a `vms-kvm-t0-csonic` testbed:
```
pytest tests/test_nbr_health.py::test_neighbors_health
```

Manual verification of the health logic against a live testbed (4 cSONiC neighbors) — each returns healthy where it previously reported "unknown":
```
csonic_vms6-1_VM0100: HEALTHY
csonic_vms6-1_VM0101: HEALTHY
csonic_vms6-1_VM0102: HEALTHY
csonic_vms6-1_VM0103: HEALTHY
```

#### Description for the changelog

Recognize cSONiC (`docker-sonic-vs`) neighbors in `test_neighbors_health` by adding a `CsonicHost` branch that checks container reachability and BGP health, instead of reporting them as an unknown neighbor type.
